messages.author: 244f5e4abbc229bf
messages.subject: Namespaces in R
parts:
Hi,

I just inherited a Shiny app that's a couple thousand lines of code or so. Most of the functionality is in the server.R file. This file uses library to load in about 10 packages or so. I'm not familiar with many of the packages, so I'm curious if there is a way to determine which function in the script comes from which library. Right now, I search the function's name on google and hope that I find which package it came from, which is tedious.

Are there any good vim scripts that help with this? Or some other way R devs handle this?

Jason

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Namespaces in R
parts:
You might find something like this useful:

search()
library(ggplot2)
search()
ggFns <- ls(2) ## the second item in the search list
grep("aes", ggFns, value=TRUE)

On my system this produces:

> grep("aes", ggFns, value=TRUE)
[1] "aes" "aes_all" "aes_auto" "aes_q" "aes_string"

-- Mike

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Namespaces in R
parts:
Perhaps I should have added that once you've identified the package
containing a given function, you can find out more information about
the function via (continuing with ggplot2 as the prototype):

library(help=ggplot2)

which provides, for instance:

aes Generate aesthetic mappings that describe how
variables in the data are mapped to visual
properties (aesthetics) of geoms.

It's also sometime useful just to look at the function itself, as, for example:

> aes
function (x, y, ...)
{
aes <- structure(as.list(match.call()[-1]), class = "uneval")
rename_aes(aes)
}
<environment: namespace:ggplot2>

(This one doesn't seem particularly interesting to me.)

And I should have mentioned the use of the "getAnywhere" function,
which may be the best solution:

> getAnywhere("aes")
A single object matching ‘aes’ was found
It was found in the following places
package:ggplot2
namespace:ggplot2
with value

function (x, y, ...)
{
aes <- structure(as.list(match.call()[-1]), class = "uneval")
rename_aes(aes)
}
<environment: namespace:ggplot2>

-- Mike

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Namespaces in R
parts:
Interesting problem! I took a quick crack at parsing a file and automatically looking up packages. Here’s the attempt on a script I was working on:

# Read in the file as a single character string
scripttext = paste(readLines('inst/control_test.R'), collapse="\n")

# Use a regex for all words (including _ and . characters) preceding an opening parenthesis
# There are base functions for this but I'm used to the stringi library's syntax
library(stringi)
function_names = stri_extract_all_regex(scripttext, "\\b[\\w_\\.]+(?=\\()")[[1]]
function_names = unique(function_names)

# Use find() to get the packages. Note that it is not vectorized, so I use a sapply
# Also, all the packages have to be loaded, I've added logic to fail gracefully
# if the function isn't defined in your current environment.
dd = data.frame(fun = function_names, 
                path = sapply(function_names, function(name) {
                  path <- find(name)
                  return(ifelse(length(path) > 0, path, NA))}))

dd[order(dd$path),]

Here’s the output. The NAs are the things it missed - functions defined in the script itself that I hadn’t run, and rply, which I can called with plyr::rlply rather than loading the package.
